fact_corrections: Kiln timeline 1980–1985: years, not more than a decade; cancer diagnosis does not establish occupational medical causation.
Runye pressured by aunt and Xu Guoqiang; Tian Fujun unaware and angry on learning.
Xiaoxia helped recruitment using father’s name without his directing it, and suggested future transfer; removed claims she never intervened.
Jin Xiu proposes work at mine hospital; provincial transfer proposal belongs to Lanxiang and Wu Zhongping.
Wang Shicai saves An Suozi, not Shaoping.
Ending welcomes Shaoping with Huiying, Mingming and dog, without invented quoted dialogue or asserted marriage.
Completion May 1988, death November 1992: four years, not three; no medical causation inferred.
provenance: Corrections supplied by moon from chapter checks, integrated into full Chinese-based translation; this reviewer does not claim to have independently reread the entire novel.
interpretive_boundaries: Hard circumstances not self-created merely because judgment is one’s own.
Refusing relationship differs from deciding another person’s future; Shaoan not responsible for every later act.
Runye not blamed for his drinking/driving; divorce socially constrained, not universally legally impossible.
Disability never means inability to give, demand, or choose; interrupted debt interpretation bounded to this narrative.
Xiaoxia’s death called necessary only within proposed literary reading, not authorial fact or universal law.
Practical help acknowledged while preserving irreducibility of books and dialogue to status advancement.
Return to mine does not prove every choice unconstrained; help and mediation acknowledged.
